Md. Salim, Deputy Attorney General, instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the petitioner.  
Anisul Huq, Advocate instructed by Md. Abu Siddique, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the Respondents.

The State ------ Petitioner
VS
A.K.M. Rafiqul Islam ------ Respondent.
full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim J: This application under Article 103 of the Constitution of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh is directed against the judgment and order dated the 29th day of October, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 6416 of 2009 making the Rule absolute. 

 2. The facts involved in the case, in short, are that the accused-petitioner and the father of victim are neighbours and there had been rivalry in between them relating to erecting boundary wall. It has been stated that while the father of victim began to erect boundary wall in his house, some miscreants at the instruction of the accused petitioner interrupted the father of the victim to erect boundary wall and demanded Tk. 5 lacs to him otherwise they threatened him to be killed. On the date of occurrence while the victim Kamrul Islam alias Momin was on the way to his college, at the instance of accused A.K.M. Refiqul Islam, the FIR named accused persons along with some unknown miscreants have gunned down the victim and left him on road with critical injuries and thereafter, the eldest brother of the victim took him to the Dhaka Medical College Hospital wherein the duty doctor in duty referred the victim to chest hospital and the surgical operation of the victim was conducted thereon. Thereafter, the victim was again referred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital wherein the doctor in duty declared him dead. 

 3. After investigation police submitted charge sheet on 13.05.2007 against five accused persons and recommended to discharge the accused petitioner along with other 21 accused persons from the case. The informant of the case filed a naraji petition in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka who has directed further investigation by Detective Branch of police and accordingly, the case was further investigated by the inspector of police D.B. DMP, Dhaka and after completion of further investigation submitted supplementary charge sheet being No. 49 dated 02.03.2008 under Section 302/34/109 of the Penal Code again seven accused persons and also recommended to discharge the accused petitioner along with 20 other accused persons from the case as no prima-facie case has been made out against them. The informant being aggrieved filed another naraji petition in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka who passed an order for judicial inquiry and in course of judicial inquiry, the Magistrate examined 9 witnesses and submitted judicial inquiry report in the Court of Chief Metropolitan  Magistrate, Dhaka who took cognizance of the case against the petitioner along with 8 other accused persons under Section 302/34 of the Penal Code but did not make any comment as to the other non-sent up accused persons. 

 4. Mr. Md. Salim, learned Deputy Attorney General, appearing for the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division while passing the impugned judgment and order enlarging accused respondent on bail failed to appreciate that the gravity of offence under Section 302/34/109 of the Penal Code now pending in the Court of Druto Bichar Tribunal  No. 3. Dhaka and if at the stage accused respondent is allowed to go on bail he will threaten the prosecution witnesses as because he is police personnel and has connection with terrorist group hence the purpose of the case will be frustrated. The learned Deputy Attorney General further submitted that there is strong prima-facie case and specific overt act against the accused respondent which has already been proved by the prosecution witnesses who have corroborated with each other hence the prosecution having been able to prove its case beyond all shadow of reasonable doubt and at this stage the impugned judgment and-order of bail would create obstacle in the way of free-fair trial.
